title: fix(rest)!: the import doors honour a control opt-out only for the system principal
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#24348

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Basis for the Clause-② line (copied from the claim, `6252062987`): a narrowing. The import door stops accepting an opt-out from an unentitled caller, and nothing newly accepted or exported is added.

## What changes

The two import doors, `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import` and `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import/jobs`, read two request flags that take an app's declared business controls off every row they write:

- `runAutomations: false` makes the runner write with `skipAutomations`, so no metadata-bound hook and no record-change trigger runs (an approval flow and a closed-record freeze hook among them).
- `treatAsHistorical: true` makes the runner write with `skipStateMachine` and `preserveAudit`, so the object's `state_machine` rule is skipped and supplied audit and read-only values are kept.

**Who may opt out:** only the system principal, `ExecutionContext.isSystem === true`, which is an in-process caller such as a seed or migration job.

**What everyone else gets:** every other caller, every signed-in user and administrator included, gets `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` in the ADR-0112 envelope when it sends either opt-out. `error.details` is `{ object, refused }`, where `refused` names the opt-outs it sent. The message names the flags, what each removes, and who may send them. The doors ask before the body is parsed, so a refused request writes no row and creates no import job. A dry run that sends an opt-out is refused too. An object the API does not expose keeps its `404` ahead of the refusal.

**What stays as it was:** a request that omits both keys, or sends `runAutomations: true` or `treatAsHistorical: false`, imports exactly as before, with every control in force. The schema shape and both defaults do not move. `runImport` in `@objectstack/core` is unchanged, so in-process callers keep their own settings.

The refusal is loud by design. A caller that asked for a silent load must learn it did not get one, so the flag is never silently ignored.

## The predicate reused (premise verified first)

No permission key, capability name or config switch is added. The gate reuses the platform's existing answer to "who may get past an app's business controls", which is the system principal:

- `packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts:114`, `refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart`: the elevated self-triggered start door (#22310) admits `executionContext?.isSystem === true` and nobody else. A platform administrator's session is refused there too.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts:502`: the approval record lock exempts `isSystem` only. It deliberately has no administrator exemption: an administrator releases a locked record through the audited approval rescue, not by writing past it.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` `#insert`: the create-side read-only strip has `isSystem` as its only exemption. The maintainer's ruling of 2026-08-08 (recorded in `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`) declined to honour `preserveAudit` on create because `treatAsHistorical` arrived on an ordinary non-system import request.
- `packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts:337`: every transport entry point assembles `isSystem: false`, so no HTTP caller carries the flag.

Administrator standing (`posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`, `admin_full_access`) was measured as the alternative. It lets a caller past record access (RLS, sharing), but nothing in the tree lets it past an app's hooks, triggers, state machine or approval lock. Entitling administrators here would therefore be a new decision, not a reuse, so this PR does not make it.

## Code positions

- `packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts`
  - `readImportControlFlags` (:223) is the one reading of the two flags. `prepareImportRequest` and the gate both use it, so the gate cannot judge a different reading from the one the runner gets.
  - `importControlOptOutRefusal` (:279) is the gate. The system-principal check is at :285.
- `packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts`: both doors ask the gate after the stage-1 `enforceApiAccess` and before `prepareImportRequest`. The sync door asks at :293 and the job door at :410. The refusal is written through the shared envelope writer (`sendError` from `@objectstack/types`).
- `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`: the `runAutomations` and `treatAsHistorical` describes now say who may send the opt-out. The `runAutomations` describe no longer promises a silent bulk load to any caller, and the schema docblock's example body no longer sends `runAutomations: false`. `content/docs/references/api/export.mdx` is regenerated by `gen:docs`. `check:generated` reports all 14 artifacts up to date.
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: new row 30b anchors the new elevation read (`check:system-context-census` requires it).
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx` and `security.mdx`: the historical-import paragraphs now say the import doors admit `treatAsHistorical: true` from the system principal only.
- Two `patch` changesets, one for `@objectstack/rest` and one for `@objectstack/spec`.

## The adjacent flag: `treatAsHistorical`, gated in this PR

This was measured, not assumed. `treatAsHistorical: true` reaches `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:766` as `skipStateMachine: true, preserveAudit: true`. That removes three declared controls:

- the object's `state_machine` validation rule (`initialStates` on insert, `transitions` on update);
- on UPDATE, the static `readonly` strip for the audit family and for author-declared business read-only fields (`closed_at`, `resolved_by` and similar);
- the `updated_at` / `updated_by` stamps, which become client-preferred.

Each of those is a declared business control, so the flag gets the same gate. One other body flag changes the write context: `createMissingOptions` puts `keptOptionValues` on the write. It was measured too. It runs no hook, validation rule, state rule or approval differently, and it admits only the exact off-list option values that one import kept. Its widening was a deliberate enforce-route decision, so it is not gated here (see Acceptance notes).

## The family: every other door that reaches the runner or a skip flag

- **Sync and async import doors:** caller-chosen values. Gated here.
- **`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/import-users`** (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts:555`, :741): `runAutomations: false` is fixed server-side. The caller's `treatAsHistorical` is parsed but never forwarded to `runImport`. Not caller-chosen.
- **Connector pull** (`packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts:427`): `runAutomations: true` and `treatAsHistorical: false` are fixed. Not caller-chosen.
- **Server-side writers that set `skipAutomations` / `skipTriggers`** (the seed loader, the comment-reactions conversion, the seed-ownership claims): all of them also run as `isSystem` with fixed values.
- **MCP, the CLI, and the runtime dispatcher's `/data` domain:** none serves an import or forwards a skip flag (searched `packages/mcp/src`, `packages/cli/src`, `packages/runtime/src/domains`).
- **The import undo door, `POST /api/v1/data/import/jobs/:jobId/undo`** (`packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts:647`): its restore and delete writes always carry `skipAutomations: true, skipStateMachine: true`, and `preserveAudit` for a historical job. The value is server-chosen, not caller-chosen, so this door is not the same shape and is not gated here. It is reported with its measured reading to the seat, detail withheld, because what an undo owes an app's controls is a separate decision.

## Tests

New file: `packages/rest/src/import-control-opt-out-gate.test.ts`. It drives the real routes over a real `ObjectQL`, the real protocol and sqlite `:memory:`, and asserts behaviour only. The fixtures are two metadata-bound hooks: an approval gate (`beforeInsert` marks a new deal `approval_status: 'pending'`) and a closed-record freeze (`beforeUpdate` refuses a change to a stored `closed` case). There are 16 cases:

- **A signed-in caller who is not the system principal**, on both doors:
  - `runAutomations: false` on an approval-gated insert is refused `403`, with no row and no job;
  - `runAutomations: false` on an update of a frozen record is refused `403`, and the record is unchanged;
  - `treatAsHistorical: true` is refused `403` the same way;
  - both opt-outs together are named together in `details.refused`.
- **Edges:**
  - a dry run with the opt-out is refused;
  - a hidden object keeps its `404`.
- **Positive controls:**
  - the same caller without the opt-out imports on both doors with both controls in force: the deal lands `pending`, and the frozen case's row is refused and unchanged;
  - explicit `runAutomations: true` / `treatAsHistorical: false` are not opt-outs.
- **The system principal keeps the opt-out:**
  - `runAutomations: false` writes past both controls on both doors;
  - `treatAsHistorical: true` is admitted.

**Ablation** at `0b764a4ab`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The subject resolves from `src` by relative import, so no build is involved. The mutation turned the gate's `if (refused.length === 0) return undefined;` into `>= 0` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `7f349a61f36d` to `e58774c610f7`). Result: **9 failed, 7 passed**. Exactly the nine refusal pins went red. The hidden-object 404, the positive controls and the system-principal cases stayed green. Restore: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**The pin sweep.** Every test that sent an opt-out through a door as a non-system caller was found by `git grep` over every file that names either flag. The tests that call `runImport` directly are untouched, because the gate is at the door. Each swept test keeps its subject:

- `import-integration.test.ts` (3 sites) and `import-dryrun-parity.test.ts` (2): the fixtures bind no automation, so the flag changed nothing. It is dropped.
- `import-job-integration.test.ts`: the historical-undo case now creates its historical job as the system principal. The undo is still the member's.
- dogfood `import-reference-exposure`, `import-user-field-target` and `validation-message-locale`: the fixtures bind no automation, so the flag is dropped.
- dogfood `organization-update-door`: the `treatAsHistorical` request is now refused `403` at the door. The same row without the flag still meets the guard's own per-row `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- dogfood `comment-thread-parent-pair`: the member's historical import is refused `403` and the pair is untouched. Without the flag, the member's update still stores the thread's pair. The engine-side `preserveAudit` half is held in `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-parent-pair.integration.test.ts`.

## Tests and gates (head `0b764a4ab`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 296 files, 6067 passed, 326 skipped, exit 0. Run at `9ee5f692e`; the rest sources are unchanged since, and only the new test file's typing moved.
- At `0b764a4ab`: the six import suites (`import-control-opt-out-gate`, `import-integration`, `import-dryrun-parity`, `import-job-integration`, `import-run-automations-agreement`, `import-prepare`) gave 6 files and 101 passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run typecheck` exited 0, and `check:test-typecheck` is OK with 0 ledgered files.
- `@objectstack/spec`: `export.test.ts` and `export-job-family-retirement.test.ts` gave 45 passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run typecheck` exited 0, and `check:generated` reports all 14 artifacts up to date after a rebuild.
- Dogfood, the five edited files against a rest `dist` built from this source: 5 files and 40 passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood run typecheck` exited 0 with all five files in the program (`--listFiles`).
- `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 12 changed `.ts` files: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 112 families at `0b764a4ab`. All 112 exited 0, and `--ran` reports 112 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED and 0 UNRUN. In the first pass, `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` before the builds and went green after. `check:query-options-erasure` caught one untyped options bag in the new test, which was then fixed.
- The ten declared wide-population families (`init-service-contract`, `live-db-isolation`, `meta-type-normalized`, `optional-error-sink`, `resume-authority-declared`, `runner-env-posture`, `settings-bind-window`, `startup-registry-verdict`, `verify-stand-in`, `wildcard-fallthrough`): all exited 0.
- `check:system-context-census`: OK, 143 read sites, 137 of 137 symbols cited.

## Consumers

- **objectstack-ai/hotcrm's dev-only `scripts/demo-staff.ts`** uses this door as the dev administrator. An administrator's session is not the system principal, so that script's opt-out is now refused and it exits by its own submitter check. The card names that as the intended loud failure.
- **objectui's Import Wizard** offers "run automations" (unchecked sends `false`) and "treat as historical" to every user. Both now answer the door's `403` for every signed-in user. Hiding or dropping those two options is objectui's surface, and this PR leaves it for the seat to raise there.

## Cross-lane declarations

- `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts` and `content/docs/references/api/export.mdx` are declared on objectstack-ai/objectstack#6017. This PR also edits the `treatAsHistorical` describe and the schema docblock's example body there, because the adjacent flag is gated in the same round.
- `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts` is **not** touched. The gate lives at the door, because every caller-chosen value enters through the two REST doors and every in-process caller fixes its own.

## Acceptance notes

- **Historical registry records are left as is.** The v17 semantic migration entry `17.import-run-automations-declared-default-corrected.ts` and the `IMPORT_RUN_AUTOMATIONS_REASON` default-change record in `packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts` still name `runAutomations: false` as the opt-out spelling. Both are records of a past release's change. The claim declares `Clause-②: no`, so this PR registers no new v18 entry.
- **`createMissingOptions` is not gated.** It admits off-list option values for the exact cells one import kept, and it skips no hook, validation rule, state rule or approval. The enforce route that widened it was a deliberate decision. Whether option membership counts as a business control the opt-out rule should cover is left to the seat.
- **One stale comment is left alone.** `import-integration.test.ts` keeps a pre-existing comment saying the min/max pre-check is "NOT gated on `runAutomations`". It predates this change and is untouched.
